newsitem.title: LEBANON: BANK HITS NEW RECORD HIGH IN BEIRUT.
newsitem.headline: BANK HITS NEW RECORD HIGH IN BEIRUT.

text.p: Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce hit a new record high of $17.75 on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Thursday and brokers said it was still the cheapest bank stock on the market.

"It is a very, very good stock. It is the cheapest in terms of the bank's profits and cashflows," Georges Abou Jaoude, Director of Lebanese Operations at Beirut finance house Financial Funds Advisors said.
"It is is going up slowly but surely. I expect it to stabilise around today's level for a while," he told Reuters.
The latest increase brought to 57 percent the total rise of the share since its December 30 listing on the exchange. It closed at $17.5 on Wednesday.
Banque Audi was unchanged at its alltime high of $23, touched for the first time last Friday while Bank of Beirut, the third bank listed, was unchanged at $3.625.
"Psychologically speaking, Audi is still the star on the market," Abou Jaoude said.
Audi has risen 53 percent above its $15 opening price on January 20.
All three bank shares traded in strong demand.

Solidere shares were mixed as A shares fell to $10.375 from $10.5 while B shares were unchanged at $10.75. on Thursday's first fixing, both A and B shares dropped briefly to $10.25 and $10.65 respectively.
"Demand for Solidere is huge with no investor willing to sell at $10.25 on the perception that the stock will rise soon," Abou Jaoude said.
Demand for both shares totalled 273,278 against a supply of 159,811 shares on the first fixing. Demand rose to 363,642 against a supply of 121,772 shares on the second fixing.
"I think these are the last days of discount on Solidere. I expect the shares to appreciate next week," he added.
Of the four industrial firms, Ciments Blancs fell to $4.75 on turnover of 198 shares from $5 on Monday. Ciments Libanais were unchanged at $1.28125 on turnover of 37,612 shares.
There was no trade in Pipemaker Eternit and tilemaker Uniceramic.
The LIBX bank index rose 0.47 percent to 148.37. The LISPI general index fell 0.23 percent to 88.13 while the BLOM general index fell 0.26 percent to 924.74.
Total BSE turnover was 155,324 shares for a value of $1,541,829 compared with Wednesday's turnover of 231,677 shares for a value of $3,241,500.
